title: Read the question into a useful model
chapter: Read the question into a useful model
goal: Worked example: positions on a ruler are not lengths.

scenes.visual: A ruler from 0 to 12 cm. A ribbon lies from the 2 cm mark to the 9 cm mark. Question: "How long is the ribbon?"
scenes.narration: Let us work one example carefully. A ribbon starts at the two centimetre mark of a ruler and ends at the nine centimetre mark. How long is the ribbon? Pause and decide what is being counted.

scenes.visual: The labels 2 and 9 lift off the ruler with tags "position", "position".
scenes.narration: The numbers two and nine are positions measured from zero. Neither of them is the length of the ribbon. We need the distance between the two positions.

scenes.visual: The seven one-centimetre gaps under the ribbon light up in turn, numbered 1 to 7.
scenes.narration: Count the gaps the ribbon covers: two to three, three to four, and so on up to eight to nine. That is seven gaps, each one centimetre long. The ribbon is seven centimetres long.

scenes.visual: Equation 9 - 2 = 7 cm appears. Above it, the eight marks from 2 to 9 flash briefly with a small "8 marks" note, then fade.
scenes.narration: Subtraction gives the same result: nine minus two is seven. Notice there are eight numbered marks from two to nine. Counting marks gives eight, which is the classic mistake. Length counts gaps, not marks.

scenes.visual: The ribbon slides to start at 0 and end at 7. Same length bracket stays.
scenes.narration: Here is a check. Slide the ribbon so it starts at zero. It now ends at seven. Sliding does not change its length, so seven centimetres makes sense.

scenes.visual: Line: "length = end position - start position". Then the notebook prompt.
scenes.narration: Length is the end position minus the start position. Now cover this solution and rebuild it yourself. Then try this: a film starts at seven fifteen and ends at nine oh five. How many minutes long is it?

notebook_exercise: A film starts at 7:15 and ends at 9:05. How many minutes long is it?
